messages:
sam: quick sync — I put up a short proposal: do we extract trace context at the ingest sidecar (OTel collector) and materialize trace_id on logs, or keep logs immutable and rely on the joiner to correlate later? RFC: https://go/rfcs/ingest-enrich

sam: pros for sidecar: consistent field name across sources, cheaper joins in query layer, enables dashboards to link log lines to spans immediately. cons: mutation at ingest, index cardinality increase.

jamie: can you paste the collector transform you had in mind? curious about perf impact.

sam: sure — here’s a minimal example I tested locally:
```yaml
processors:
  attributes/enrich_trace_id:
    actions:
      - key: trace_id
        action: insert
        from_attribute: trace.id
```
collector config uses attributes processor + resource detection. cheap per-event CPU but adds bytes.

maria: fwiw we need to be careful — some customers/logs contain PII. adding trace_id as top-level field may change retention/exports to downstream sinks (S3, gcs). need policy + opt-in flag.

kevin: +1 to opt-in. Also consider a canonical field name: we should standardize on "trace_id" (snake_case) and map variant headers (TRACEPARENT, x-trace-id) at ingress. otherwise dashboards + alerting rules become messy.

jamie: what about rollouts? can we gate via feature flag per-org? i.e. "enable_ingest_enrichment" toggle with canary on 5% tenants then ramp. dashboard UX should expose % enabled and enrichment failure rates.

sam: exactly — planned rollout: start with internal orgs, then customers on Dedicated. config key: `ingest.enrichment.enabled` in control plane. will add telemetry for enrichment_latency_ms and enriched_event_count.

ingest-bot: collector-side metric: enrich_processor.latency_p50=1.2ms, p99=9ms; enriched_events_total=124k (last 5m).

maria: another concern: exporters. If we materialize trace_id for logs, BigQuery/ES schemas will change. need migration plan + docs. Could also add as attribute instead of top-level field for sinks that preserve nested attrs.

kevin: for query performance, ES users want top-level field. we can write a pipeline that optionally promotes attribute->top-level based on sink config. add to RFC.

jamie: TL;DR: prefer collector-level enrichment but behind per-tenant opt-in + canary rollout, standardize field name, and ensure exporter compatibility and privacy controls. I can help write the rollout playbook. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — I'll update the RFC with: canonical field name, opt-in flag, collector snippet, metrics to emit, and a migration checklist for sinks. planning to put up a canary tomorrow morning.

kevin: sounds good. ping me when the canary URL is live so platform can wire dashboards and alerting.

maria: please include a short audit log entry whenever enrichment is enabled for a tenant (for compliance).

sam: noted. creating follow-up ticket: https://go/issue/INF-4921 — feel free to drop comments there.
